answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards and place a face-down set of players + 1 on the board; return the rest without looking. Put one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘number of players + 1’; ‘11 marked territories’; ‘Randomly choose one structure bonus tile’; ‘The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts’

answers.answer: Character starts at home; two workers start on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home; four mechs on Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six technology cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits in bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat ready for first placement. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and objectives (two cards).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 list mat assignments and starting pieces.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action. Normally you cannot repeat the section from last turn; Rusviet may repeat a section. If taking both actions, take top before bottom; top-row gains may pay bottom-row cost. Pay the full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefit as desired. Costs/benefits follow the Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘must move the token’; ‘bottom first is not allowed’; ‘Rusviet may repeat’; ‘First pay the full cost’

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure abilities; you retain them without control, except the Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Pay with resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it and all its resources’; ‘Resources stay on the board. Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control’

answers.answer: No: the normal Move selects up to two different units, one adjacent territory each, and the same unit cannot be selected twice. A carried worker may later move itself, or move onto a mech and be carried by its later move. All units may carry any number of resources; only mechs may additionally carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘two different units’; ‘cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice’; carried-worker rule; all units carry resources, only mechs carry workers.

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech stops and cannot move again that turn when it enters enemy-workers-only territory; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having no popularity does not prevent retreat. This is not combat. A worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops’; ‘Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero’; ‘A worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory’

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order’; worker restriction.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades. If the draw deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker; if all workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade paragraphs specify costs, choices, placement, worker condition and exhausted-deck handling.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and enter the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers exposed during production affect future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3: ‘Pay every exposed Produce cost … in full’; ‘Take new workers from the Player Mat left to right’; ‘Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions’

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box (not solid-black-bordered) to improve a top benefit and reduce a bottom cost. Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; put a chosen mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability applies from then on to character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may still pay a bottom action to get its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy and concluding sentence on paying completed actions.

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory with your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases forbidden, and only one structure total per territory. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill adds a bonus Produce territory and one bonus worker output; it cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. A Mine is your personal tunnel for all your unit movement, including Factory Move, even when enemy-controlled; enemies cannot use your buildings’ abilities.
answers.evidence: Build paragraph describes placement and permanence; Mill and Mine abilities; control exception says Mill cannot produce uncontrolled.

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section and put it permanently on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where that recruit was removed, independent of the one-time choice. When you or an immediate neighbor takes its matching bottom action, resolve active player first, then left, then right; in two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits paragraphs state placement, one-time bonuses, trigger and ordering.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and current power. Each may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including with zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers are present. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial and card values, and attacker wins ties. Each player deducts their own dial power from the track and discards every played card; card values do not cost track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3 specify simultaneous secret choices, cards, ability order, reveal, payments and tie.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory/resources and places a combat star if eligible (ordinary maximum two; Saxony unrestricted within six available). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead retreat eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie applies to its stated combat case. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 4–5 give retreats, resources, popularity, stars and loser card reward.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter only if the character remains on the token territory. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no normal action costs or mat benefits/ongoing recruit bonuses apply.
answers.evidence: Encounters: ‘After the whole Move action and all combats’; ‘If contested entry is lost … token stays’; ‘All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory’; no additional normal action costs/mat benefits.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom under the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement/stop rules apply.
answers.evidence: Factory section specifies per-player card selection timing, action use, absent benefits and bottom Move distance.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you must meet all requirements at reveal time. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star; Saxony retains the other card and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section gives timing, requirements, discards and Saxony exception.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later drops; another player's star does not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists achievements, permanence, nonblocking and sixth-star timing.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. Pending unresolved battle movement is undone: return initiating units to their territories and do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish active action, then resolve active player, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star each time; once the sixth is placed, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star paragraph specifies bottom-action sequence, pending battle undo and recruit-star order.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the example gives $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory and $2 per complete resource pair: five stars = $20; four ordinary territories plus Factory (five counted territories) = $15; 13 resources = six pairs = $12; total $47 added to held coins, before any structure bonus. Structure bonus is scored even if enemies control your structure territories. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and example say 10 popularity, five stars, four ordinary territories plus Factory, 13 resources score $20 + $21 + $12 = $53; tiebreaker list. The example arithmetic conflicts with the table's stated $3 per territory: $20 + $15 + $12 = $47.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move into any home base; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘A home base is not a territory’; entry exceptions; inactive expansion placeholders.

answers.answer: Mountain produces metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, village a worker; lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources definition and no-supply-limit sentence.

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up, carry and drop any number of resources, including mid-movement; mechs may carry your workers but never your character. Speed adds one territory to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one step, with the extra Speed step before or after it; a mech may pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move carrying rules and Speed paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘All printed tunnel territories are adjacent … by any unit’; ‘Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure’

answers.answer: Do not pay a partial Produce cost. Take a legal dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action. You must move sections even when taking no action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn’; ‘Never pay only part of a cost.’

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power on Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity on Bolster. These are bonuses on the matching top actions. You keep structure abilities even without control of their territory, so enemy occupation does not remove them; Mill is the stated control exception.
answers.evidence: Bolster/Trade paragraphs and control rule: ‘You keep those abilities even without control, except the Mill’

answers.answer: Riverwalk is for character/mechs: Rusviet to farms and villages; Crimea to farms and tundra; Nordic to forests and mountains; Polania to villages and mountains; Saxony to forests and mountains. Nordic Swim instead lets workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes, and does not help its character/mechs; it gives no lake movement.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities table and Nordic Swim description.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including its Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move. These shortcuts are for character/mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township descriptions.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or its Mine: opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery applies before combat and allows payment of one power to reduce opponent power by two, also once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Disarm and Nordic Artillery descriptions.

answers.answer: Two mechs plus three workers allow three cards with People's Army: one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total when at least one worker is present. Workers alone never fight.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: ‘Two mechs and three workers allow three cards’; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to its own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare ability description.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion spends one combat card per turn as any one resource, regardless of the card's value.
answers.evidence: Crimea Scout and Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy allows character/mechs to move to/from lakes and allows eligible units to retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home. Polania Submerge allows character/mechs to move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; it does not grant Nordic's adjacent-lake retreat exception. When leaving a lake, workers require a mech to move off, and carried workers or resources cannot be left behind on the lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy, Polania Submerge, and lake-carried pieces paragraph.

answers.answer: Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not protect against popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie description states both cases.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first gain can pay the second option's cost. The summary does not state that two cards are drawn; it describes one drawn card and up to two options on it.
answers.evidence: Faction table: ‘choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost’; Encounters: draw a card.

answers.answer: Yes, a character entering an encounter token territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. Resolve encounters after the whole Move action and all combats, only if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Move encounter rule and Encounters section; Factory says normal movement/stop restrictions apply.

answers.answer: Combat-card count is public but contents secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but a player need not reveal their total coin value. During combat players may conceal whether they committed cards until reveal.
answers.evidence: Setup information paragraph.

answers.answer: Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable in informal, unenforceable agreements; tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances. A payment cannot cancel combat after movement has put units onto opposing units; combat must occur, though bribes may influence the outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: ‘Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable’; agreements unenforceable; negotiation cannot cancel initiated combat.

answers.answer: At popularity 0–6, each star pays $3, territory $2, resource pair $1; at 7–12, $4, $3, $2; at 13–18, $5, $4, $3. Controlled lakes count, home bases do not. Only complete pairs score; an odd leftover resource is ignored.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and scoring paragraph.

answers.answer: For adjacency tiles, count unique features once across all structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Encounters count at printed locations even after their tokens are removed. Tunnel counts are unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines. Lakes count unique lakes. Payout for each of these three tiles: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; tunnel 6 $9; lakes/encounters 6–7 $9. Zero qualifying features scores zero.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table and following rules specify unique counts, removed encounters, printed tunnels, river rule and payouts.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels counts printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures in a row scores only the longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures on farms/tundras counts qualifying structures combined: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table entries for these three tiles.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity for each enemy worker forced to retreat, including a worker carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 5 explicitly includes workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.

answers.answer: No. A placed star is permanent, but current popularity determines final scoring, so a popularity star does not protect the current popularity level or scoring tier. Another player's star never blocks the same goal; each player's achievement may be awarded.
answers.evidence: Stars paragraph: ‘A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later drops; current popularity still determines final scoring’; ‘Other players’ stars never block a goal.’

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions clockwise in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. This determines immediate left/right neighbors whose corresponding bottom actions can trigger ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–3 and Ongoing recruits neighbor-trigger rule.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move terrain paragraph defines river/lake and lake entry.

answers.answer: No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: ‘Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud.’

answers.answer: There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.’

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘After the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, the next clockwise player may begin their turn while the current player decides…’

answers.answer: No. You may take each section's top action once and then its bottom action once; you cannot return to the top action after the bottom. A section cannot be taken twice in one turn. Rusviet may repeat a section from last turn, including its Factory card, which is not a second action within the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure specifies top once, bottom once and no return; Rusviet may repeat a section from last turn.

answers.answer: You may alternatively gain $1 from the normal unupgraded Move action.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: ‘Alternatively gain $1.’

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat. A worker retreating to its home base does not return to the Player Mat either, so it cannot cover a Produce cost again.
answers.evidence: Produce: ‘Workers never return to the Player Mat’; forced worker retreat goes to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power, zero popularity, or both.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You may attack with zero power/popularity.’

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit, though you cannot place more ordinary combat stars beyond the two-star limit.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.’

answers.answer: No to declining all options or choosing an unaffordable option: a faction without Meander must choose one affordable option, and unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected. Yes, you may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters states must choose one affordable option, unaffordable options cannot be selected, and benefits may be taken as little as desired.

answers.answer: No turn-order selection: combatants simultaneously and secretly choose their dials and optional cards. They reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: ‘simultaneously and secretly choose’; ‘Reveal simultaneously.’

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.’

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as its goal is achieved; it cannot be declined or delayed, and the sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but when revealed on your turn you must meet all requirements at that moment.
answers.evidence: Stars: ‘Place a star as soon as you achieve’; Sixth star ends immediately. Objectives: ‘You may wait’ to reveal.

answers.answer: Normally no character, mech or worker may cross rivers or enter lakes. The summary then describes faction/mech ability exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes.’

answers.answer: No. The recruit is placed permanently on an open one-time recruit bonus on the Faction Mat and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: ‘put it permanently’; ‘It cannot later move.’

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not resolve it or remove the token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: ‘Only a character triggers an encounter.’

answers.answer: While controlled, the Mill adds one bonus Produce territory in addition to the normal selected territories. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker, and each actual worker there also produces normally. With no actual worker, the Mill can still produce one terrain-table token, provided the territory is controlled.
answers.evidence: Produce: controlled Mill provides an additional territory; Mill counts as a worker; can produce without an actual worker. Control rule excludes uncontrolled Mill production.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control after your last unit leaves if you have no structure.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: control is by unit or structure with no enemy unit; resources stay on board but are not listed as control.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Upgrade — oil’; ‘Deploy — metal’; ‘Build — wood’; ‘Enlist — food.’
